question: Should OpenClaw permit `gateway.auth.mode: "none"` on non-loopback/private-ingress Gateway binds, and if so what explicit guard or acknowledgement boundary is required?
rationale: The request moves protection of a powerful Gateway operator surface from OpenClaw-managed auth to external network controls, which needs maintainer security/product intent rather than automated repair judgment.

options.title: Keep Fail-Closed Reachable Binds
options.body: Maintain the current token/password/trusted-proxy requirement for non-loopback Gateway binds and document supported private-ingress alternatives.

options.title: Sponsor Dangerous Private-Ingress Opt-In
options.body: Add a named explicit no-auth private-ingress policy with warnings, audit coverage, docs, and tests instead of a validation-free bypass.

options.title: Close As Not Planned
options.body: If maintainers reject this trust model in core, close this issue and point users to token/password, trusted-proxy, or verified Tailscale flows.

recommendation.title: Keep Fail-Closed Reachable Binds
recommendation.body: Maintain the current token/password/trusted-proxy requirement for non-loopback Gateway binds and document supported private-ingress alternatives.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle has the strongest recent history on the exposed Gateway auth boundary and adjacent fail-closed hardening.
